bill.constitutionalAuthorityStatementText:
[Congressional Record Volume 169, Number 51 (Tuesday, March 21, 2023)]
[House]
From the Congressional Record Online through the Government Publishing Office [www.gpo.gov]
By Ms. JAYAPAL:
H.R. 1679.
Congress has the power to enact this legislation pursuant
to the following:
This bill is enacted pursuant to the power granted to
Congress under Article I of the United States Constitution
and its subsequent amendments, and further clarified and
interpreted by the Supreme Court of the United States.
The single subject of this legislation is:
Bans Members of Congress and their spouses from owning and
trading individual stocks, bonds, commodities, futures, and
other securities including an interest in a hedge fund, a
derivative, an option, or other complex investment vehicle.
[Page H1302]

latestAction.text: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on Agriculture, House Administration, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

bill.title: Bipartisan Ban on Congressional Stock Ownership Act of 2023
